combat_history.event: Major export contracts signed with the UAE and later Saudi Arabia and Iraq.
combat_history.significance: Established Cheongung as a flagship South Korean defence export.

modernization.description: Higher-performance interceptors and integration with the long-range L-SAM upper tier.
modernization.impact: Deepens Korea's indigenous layered missile defence.

vulnerabilities.context: Needs L-SAM and Patriot above it for full coverage.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerable to mass short-range ballistic-missile salvos.
vulnerabilities.context: North Korea fields very large numbers of SRBMs.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Mid-tier defence of South Korean airspace and forces against aircraft and short-range ballistic missiles.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Layered within KAMD beneath Patriot and L-SAM.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Patriot is the imported higher-capability layer; Cheongung is the indigenous mid-tier reducing import dependence.
Comparable medium-range SAM in China's layered IADS.
A European medium-to-long-range SAM with similar BMD ambitions.

doctrine.role: Indigenous medium-range air- and missile-defence system; the mid-tier of Korea's KAMD.
doctrine.employment: Hit-to-kill interception of aircraft and short-range ballistic missiles under Patriot and L-SAM.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Sovereign, mass-producible interception against a missile-heavy adversary.
doctrine.threat_context: Defends South Korea against the large North Korean SRBM force and anchors a growing export business.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read with Patriot (above) and against China's HQ-16 and Europe's Aster 30.
